---
description: Build Phase 5 — Inventory on the P2 kernel: items, UoM, barcodes, warehouses, append-only stock moves with derived quantities, weighted-average costing in posting order with a negative-stock policy, adjustments, transfers through in-transit, counts, valuation and movement reports; stock valuation == inventory GL balance at any date
---
Implement **Phase 5** as specified in `docs/Vinea_ERP_Master_Plan_v5.md` §5 (P5), §6 invariant 3, §B.2 (IBT disposition, project dimension on stock moves) and Appendix C (navigation contract, Inventory rows).

Inventory is built the same way the ledger and the subledger were: an **append-only move table is the truth, everything else is derived and provably so**. `stock_moves` is to inventory what `journal_lines` is to the GL. No quantity or cost column that is not a verifiable cache of moves. If you find yourself updating `qty_on_hand` from a document handler, stop — that is the v4 design this rebuild exists to delete.

Two mandatory **STOP for owner approval** gates: after step 2 and after step 5. Report and wait for an explicit go-ahead. Never continue past a report on a "Continue to iterate?" prompt.

Where the plan leaves a choice open, decide, implement, and list it under "Decisions worth review" in that step's report, as P1–P4 did.

## Preconditions (already built — consume, never re-implement)

- **Tenancy and auth (P1):** httpOnly cookie sessions, `CompanyMembership`, every tenant table `ENABLE` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` with `FOR ALL` policies carrying `WITH CHECK`, RLS linter tests, audited service calls with a real `actor`, dev as non-superuser `vinea_app`, migrations through `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` only (`make migrate-check`; the P4 wipe happened because `DATABASE_URL` was assumed to drive Alembic — it does not).
- **Ledger kernel (P2):** PostingEngine is the only GL writer (`app.posting_engine='on'` trigger). Journal lines are signed amounts with dimensions including `item_id` — the item dimension already exists on `journal_lines`; use it, do not add a parallel one. Gapless `document_sequences`, derived `period_balances` + verify function, half-up rounding to `currency.decimal_places` (RWF = 0), immutability triggers, frozen-base reversals, period lookup with `FOR SHARE`, `assert_ledger_invariants` as the standing acceptance contract.
- **Subledger machinery (P4):** `journal_entries.module`; the control-account guard as a `control_account_modules` `(module, control_type)` registry enforced in the engine **and** by DB trigger (VN007), default deny; the dimension-required check (VN008). P4 already seeded a registry row for the inventory module and an item-required rule that is a no-op today because no INV-typed accounts exist — P5 makes it real. `gl_settings` keys for account defaults; `gl_transaction_types.module` (`gl`, `ar`, `ap` so far); `partner_documents` / `partner_document_lines` — **leave them untouched**; the batch pattern (one header, N lines, one `Idempotency-Key`, refused whole); `verify_open_items()` as the model for a verifiable cache; the `jobs` table (bytes in row, 7-day retention, listing never selects the bytes column, reaper for orphaned `running` rows, WeasyPrint libs installed in CI); `docs/approvals.md`; nightly `HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=deep` workflow; `make db-reset` seeding Rugari Wines E2E and Kivu Traders E2E.
- **Frontend (P3/P4):** tokens and primitives, shell rendering the full Appendix C tree with later phases disabled and phase-tagged, `DocumentWorkspace` + `LineGrid` (keyboard model parametrised across all navigable columns — keep it that way for new columns) including **batch mode**, IndexedDB drafts keyed by draft UUID as `Idempotency-Key`, inline `field_errors`, next-intl with every string externalised, `formatMoney`, the "Include zero balances" toggle convention, the Rename screen pattern with history, print layouts and CSV, posting **preview before Post** (allocation screen), Playwright e2e on `docker compose` with `E2E_PASSWORD` from env, `axe` in CI.
- **Process rules that are now standing, not optional:** a screen is not done until a test has opened it with data and a committed screenshot shows rows (copilot-instructions rule 13 — six P3 defects were on screens nobody opened); delegated verification attaches raw command output or it is not evidence; every regression test is proven sensitive by reverting the fix and watching it fail; "fails locally, passes in CI" is environment drift to fix, not accept; a generator that cannot produce the shape where the risk lives is not a guard.
- **Before step 6:** confirm in the step-1 report whether issues #9 (axe on all screens + `/design`) and #6 (i18n back-fill) are closed on `main`. If either is open, it is the first PR of this phase — P5 screens are not built on top of known accessibility and i18n debt.

## Out of scope — do not build

Item lines on partner documents, COGS on invoices, `StockSold` (all P6, together with SO/PO/GRN, three-way match, backorders, landed cost, kit breakup); IBT requisition → approve → issue workflow (B.2: backlog — P5 ships direct transfers only); serial, batch or lot tracking; FIFO/LIFO/standard costing; per-warehouse average cost; price lists (one default selling price only); reorder automation, MRP (P12); sales analysis and slow movers (P10 — leave their nav tags); VSDC item classification or any `fiscal_*` column on items (P7); POS tills (P11); warehouse-level GL account overrides beyond the in-transit rule in decision 6.

## Decisions locked for this phase — implement exactly

1. **Stock moves are the ledger.** `stock_moves`: company, item, warehouse, `move_date`, `period_id`, signed `quantity` in the item's base UoM (`NUMERIC(20,6)`), `unit_cost` (`NUMERIC(20,10)`, nullable for revaluations), signed `value` in base currency rounded half-up to base decimals, `journal_entry_id`, `source_doc_type`, `source_doc_id`, `source_line_id`, `project_id`, `cost_provisional`, and a posting-order sequence. Append-only under the same immutability trigger discipline as `journal_lines`. `stock_balances(item, warehouse) {quantity, value}` and `item_cost_state(item) {average_cost, last_positive_average_cost}` are caches written only by the stock service, with `verify_stock_balances()` recomputing both from moves — the `open_amount` pattern from P4. Every as-of query reconstructs from moves.
2. **Inventory accounts are control accounts.** The inventory account and the in-transit account carry `control_type='INV'` (match the type name P4 seeded in the registry). Only `module='inventory'` may post to them; every such line carries `item_id`; a manual journal against them fails `control_account_direct_posting`. Consequence, same as AR/AP: opening stock cannot arrive as a GL journal — it comes through the inventory journal batch with an opening-balance type. Say so in the onboarding notes.
3. **One stock document → one journal entry**, `module='inventory'`, posted in the same transaction as the moves, source links both ways, one inventory-account line per move (with `item_id`, the warehouse's `branch_id`, and `project_id` when tagged) against the contra account from the transaction type. No document posts moves without an entry or an entry without moves.
4. **Costing: weighted average per item per company, base currency, posting order.** A backdated receipt changes the average from its posting time onward; earlier-posted issues are never restated — immutability and closed periods outrank date order, and this is the rule the DoD tape tests. Average = Σvalue / Σquantity across all locations, to 6 dp, while Σquantity > 0; otherwise the last positive average. Value rules, all half-up to base decimals: receipt value = round(qty × unit cost); issue value = round(qty × average), **except** an issue that takes a location to exactly zero takes that location's remaining value; the receive leg of a transfer carries the dispatched value frozen; a revaluation is a move with quantity 0 and a non-zero value. A ±1 minor-unit shift of the average after a location empties is a rounding consequence, not a bug — the invariant is on value.
5. **Negative stock policy, per company.** `block` (default): an issue that would take a location below zero fails `insufficient_stock`, evaluated per location in posting order. `allow`: the issue posts at the last positive average, the move is flagged `cost_provisional`, and the item enquiry and transaction report expose a provisional filter. No retroactive correction when a later receipt restores the quantity; the flag is the review trail.
6. **Transfers move through a system in-transit warehouse.** One `is_in_transit` warehouse per company, created by seed, mapped to `inventory_in_transit_account`, not selectable on any other document. Dispatch posts source → transit; receive posts transit → destination; each leg is its own posting with the branch of its physical warehouse. The default UI action "Transfer now" runs both in one transaction. A dispatched, unreceived transfer is stock in transit on the valuation report and value in the in-transit account — the invariant covers it.
7. **Counts are snapshot-based and refuse stale lines.** A session per warehouse freezes `system_quantity` per line at `snapshot_at`; counted quantity is entered per line; variance = counted − snapshot. A line whose item/warehouse has a move posted after the snapshot is `stale`; Process refuses with `count_line_stale` until that line is re-snapshotted and recounted. Process posts one count-variance document with every non-zero variance (losses and gains both at the current average) and moves the session to Completed. The screen previews the posting before Process, like the allocation screen.
8. **Items, UoM, barcodes.** `item_type` stock | service | non_stock; only stock items ever have moves. `uom_categories` with a base unit; `uoms` with a `factor_to_base` (`NUMERIC(20,10)`) and `decimal_places`; an item has a base UoM; entry in any UoM of the same category converts to base at 6 dp before it becomes a move. `item_barcodes`: many per item, each with a UoM and pack quantity, unique per company; `GET /inventory/items/lookup` resolves code or barcode. Item carries default inventory, COGS and sales accounts and default sales/purchase tax codes (COGS, sales and tax defaults are data for P6 — no behaviour here) and one `selling_price` with a `price_includes_tax` flag.
9. **Transaction types reuse `gl_transaction_types`** with `module='inventory'` and a `kind`: `adjustment_in`, `adjustment_out`, `revaluation`, `transfer`, `count_variance`, `opening_balance`; each carries its contra account. Users add their own types (Damaged, Samples, …) of an existing kind with their own contra — that is what the Maintenance screen is for. The journal batch is the P4 batch pattern: one header, N lines (item, warehouse, signed quantity or zero-quantity value for revaluation, unit cost on increases, transaction type, contra override, project, description), one idempotency key, refused whole on any line failure. This is the go-live opening-stock path.
10. **Settings on the existing mechanism.** New `gl_settings` keys: `inventory_account`, `inventory_adjustment_account`, `inventory_in_transit_account`, `stock_count_variance_account` (allowed to equal adjustment), `cogs_account` (seeded now, used in P6). `negative_stock_policy` and `default_warehouse_id` on the same settings mechanism — do not introduce a second settings store.
11. **Reversal** = kernel reversal plus reversing moves at the original values in posting order, subject to the negative-stock policy (a receipt whose quantity has since been issued cannot be reversed under `block`). A processed count stays Completed and links to the reversal.
12. **Numbering and idempotency.** Adjustment, journal batch, transfer and count each get a `document_sequences` doc type with a prefix in the P4 style; `Idempotency-Key` on every post, dispatch, receive and process.
13. **Primitives for P6.** `receive_stock()` and `issue_stock()` in the stock service, emitting `StockReceived` / `StockIssued` events through the PostingEngine, callable with any `source_doc`. Adjustments, transfers and counts are their only callers in P5; P6 wires documents to them without changing them.

## Build order — commit after each step with green checks

1. **Masters.** Tables, RLS, services, endpoints: `uom_categories`, `uoms`, `items`, `item_barcodes`, `warehouses` (code, name, `branch_id`, `is_default`, `is_in_transit`, `is_active`), inventory `gl_transaction_types`, the five `gl_settings` keys, policy settings, permissions in the existing constant style (setup, post, count-process, view, rename), Rename Item Code with history on the P3/P4 rename pattern. Rwanda seed pack: inventory, adjustment and in-transit accounts if the COA template lacks them (mark them `INV` control), UoM categories Count/Weight/Volume/Length with base units, warehouse Main on the main branch plus the in-transit warehouse, the seeded transaction types. Back-fill migration for existing tenants, and the back-fill test from P4: provision at the pre-P5 revision, upgrade to head, assert every key, account, UoM, warehouse and type lands non-null. Migration applies from zero, `alembic check` clean.

2. **Stock ledger, costing engine, posting contract.** `stock_moves`, caches, `verify_stock_balances()`, the costing rules of decision 4, the policy of decision 5, `receive_stock()` / `issue_stock()`, the INV control type wired into the P4 registry and trigger so the item-required check now fires. Extend the invariant suite with `assert_stock_invariants`: for every INV account at any date, Σ `stock_balances.value` of its locations == the account balance (per branch as well); Σ moves == every cache; average == value / quantity wherever quantity > 0; a location with quantity 0 has value 0; no non-provisional negative quantity under `block`; every INV journal line carries `item_id` and has exactly one move. Hypothesis: a random sequence of receipts, issues, transfers, revaluations and reversals across two warehouses, at a 0-dp and a 2-dp base currency, asserting the whole suite after every step — including large quantities where a 6-dp average times quantity drifts from the true value, which is the shape the flush rule exists for. **STOP.** Report the schema, the posting map per kind, the costing rules as implemented, the invariant suite and its output. Wait for approval before building documents.

3. **Adjustments and journal batches.** Adjustment document (single item, increase / decrease / revaluation by transaction type) and the batch endpoint on the P4 batch pattern, including opening balances; reversal per decision 11. Period enforcement inherited from the kernel; a document dated in a closed period is rejected before any move exists.

4. **Transfers and counts.** Transfer document with dispatch / receive / transfer-now; count sessions with snapshot, line entry, stale detection, preview, process, cancel. Property tests: dispatch → receive returns the item to the same total value; a count processed against a stale line is impossible; transfer-now under `block` with insufficient source quantity fails whole.

5. **Enquiry, reports, the costing tape — backend.** Item enquiry (balances per warehouse, moves with running quantity and value, drill to journal entry, provisional filter). Reports with server pagination and as-of reconstruction by document date: Movement (opening, moves, closing per item × warehouse over a range), Transaction (move listing, filters, drill), Valuation (as-of, per warehouse, item totals from the frozen values, zero-quantity lines off by default), Count (sessions, lines, variances, link to the posted document). Assert valuation as-of any date == inventory account balance as-of that date, per branch. Then the **costing tape** as an acceptance test in the RWF-base company, one stock item, warehouses Main and Depot, with the expected column as literals worked by hand in a comment — never computed by the code under test:

   | # | Action | Expected after the step |
   |---|---|---|
   | 1 | Opening batch: 10 @ 100, Main | Main 10 / 1 000 · avg 100 |
   | 2 | Adjustment in: 10 @ 121, Main | Main 20 / 2 210 · avg 110.5 |
   | 3 | Adjustment out: 7, Main | value 774 (773.5 half-up) · Main 13 / 1 436 · avg 110.461538 |
   | 4 | Adjustment in dated **before** step 3: 5 @ 130, Main | Main 18 / 2 086 · avg 115.888889 · step 3 unchanged at 774 |
   | 5 | Transfer now 6, Main → Depot | value 695 · Main 12 / 1 391 · Depot 6 / 695 · avg unchanged |
   | 6 | Adjustment out: 12, Main (empties it) | value 1 391 (flush) · Main 0 / 0 · Depot 6 / 695 · avg 115.833333 |
   | 7 | Count Depot, counted 5 → variance −1, Process | value 116 · Depot 5 / 579 · avg 115.8 |
   | 8a | Adjustment out: 6, Depot, policy `block` | `insufficient_stock`, nothing posted |
   | 8b | Same, policy `allow` | value 695 · Depot −1 / −116 · move `cost_provisional` · avg stays 115.8 |
   | 9 | Adjustment in: 3 @ 150, Depot | Depot 2 / 334 · avg 167 · no correction of 8b |

   After every row: `assert_stock_invariants` and `assert_ledger_invariants` green, inventory account == Σ location values, Main/Depot branch balances match the per-warehouse values. **STOP.** Report with the tape output table and the invariant suite output. Wait for approval before any UI work.

6. **Maintenance UI.** Inventory items (with barcodes and UoM), Warehouses, Transaction types (filtered by `module`), Variable barcodes, Units of measure categories, Inventory defaults, Rename Item Code — in the owner's order under Maintenance → Inventory. Clear the `P5` tag on each nav item as its screen lands; each screen opened by a test with data and a committed screenshot.

7. **Transaction UI.** Adjustments on `DocumentWorkspace`; Journal batches on `LineGrid` batch mode restricted to the module (item typeahead by code, barcode or description showing quantity on hand at the chosen warehouse, UoM column with conversion shown, unit cost on increases only); Warehouse transfers with Transfer now / Dispatch / Receive; Inventory count: start session → enter counts (keyboard-first, one row per item, uncounted rows visibly distinct) → review variances with the posting preview → Process. Drafts keyed by draft UUID as `Idempotency-Key`. Errors inline: `insufficient_stock` lands on the quantity cell, `count_line_stale` on the line.

8. **Enquiries and Reports UI.** Item enquiry with drill-down warehouse → move → journal entry and the provisional filter. Reports in the owner's order: Movement, Count, Transaction, Valuation — print layout and CSV as in P3/P4; Sales analyses and Slow movers stay tagged P10.

9. **Tests and CI.** Playwright e2e on `docker compose`: create a UoM category and unit → create a stock item with a barcode → add a second warehouse → post the opening batch → adjustment in → transfer → count with a variance → process → valuation report total equals the inventory account in the GL report → movement report shows the running balance → negative-stock block fires, the policy switch allows it and the enquiry shows the provisional flag → reverse the adjustment and watch the value return. Credentials from env. Backend suite, `alembic check`, ruff, all frontend jobs including `axe` green. Sensitivity pass on the final SHA: revert the INV guard, the flush rule and the stale-line refusal one at a time, name the test that catches each. README → Phase 5 complete, `docs/p5-final-report.md`, approvals rows in `docs/approvals.md`, Appendix C test updated for the cleared P5 tags.

## Definition of Done (all must be true)

The costing tape reproduces every expected value above to the rounding rule, including the posting-order treatment of the backdated receipt; `assert_stock_invariants` passes, so stock valuation equals the inventory GL balance at any date and per branch, with in-transit accounted for; nothing but the inventory module can post to an INV account and every such line carries an item; quantities and costs are derived from moves and `verify_stock_balances()` reports no drift; the negative-stock policy blocks by default and flags under `allow`; a stale count line cannot be processed; every P5 item in the Appendix C tree is live, untagged, opened by a test with data and shown in a committed screenshot; nothing writes to the ledger outside the PostingEngine; every audited call passes a real actor; CI green on backend and frontend. Final report: what landed, screenshots of the journal batch, the count review with its preview and the valuation report, decisions worth review, and any plan deviations with reasons.
